Run code
async () => {
  // Aggregate the shared kyoto_image collection by source article to verify 3 images per attraction and detect lost updates.
  try {
    const res = await tools.data_store({ action: "list", table: "kyoto_image", limit: 1000 });
    const rows = (res && res.rows) || [];
    const byPage = {};
    const urls = new Set();
    for (const r of rows) {
      const d = r.data || {};
      const key = (d.pageUrl || "unknown").replace(/^https?:\/\/en\.wikipedia\.org\/wiki\//, "");
      byPage[key] = byPage[key] || { count: 0, srcs: [] };
      byPage[key].count++;
      byPage[key].srcs.push(d.src);
      urls.add(d.src);
    }
    return {
      ok: true,
      totalRows: rows.length,
      uniqueImages: urls.size,
      groups: Object.entries(byPage).map(([k, v]) => ({ article: k, count: v.count, images: v.srcs.map(s => String(s).split("/").slice(-1)[0].split("?")[0]) }))
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: String(e && e.message || e) };
  }
}

Done — kyoto_image gallery: 15 images, 3 per attraction

I created the gallery and ran 5 sub-tasks in parallel (one per attraction), all writing into the same image collection kyoto_image. All five finished in ~90 seconds, and I verified the final table: 15 rows, 15 unique image URLs, exactly 3 per attraction.

What's in the gallery

Attraction Source article Images collected
Fushimi Inari Shrine Fushimi Inari-taisha Torii path with lantern (infobox), Senbon Torii tunnel, rōmon main gate
Kinkaku-ji Kinkaku-ji Golden Pavilion water mirror (infobox), pavilion + garden/pond, pavilion over the lake
Kiyomizu-dera Kiyomizu-dera Main hall with the wooden stage (infobox), November 2016 view, 2024 view
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove Bamboo Forest (Kyoto) + 2 supplementary pages Bamboo path (infobox), Sagano bamboo forest, bamboo grove vertical shot
Nijo Castle Nijō Castle Kara-mon gate to Ninomaru Palace (infobox), stone walls & moat, Ninomaru garden pond

Each sub-task visually verified its picks with read_image before saving and excluded maps, plans/diagrams, seals, and portraits. I also re-verified independently: all 3 Arashiyama assets plus one image from each of the other four attractions — every one clearly depicts its stated attraction (torii tunnel, golden pavilion with reflection, Kiyomizu stage, Nijo Kara-mon).

Notes and limitations

  • Arashiyama provenance differs from the others. The dedicated article "Bamboo Forest (Kyoto)" contains only one grove photo, so that sub-task supplemented with one image each from the broader Arashiyama article and a Wikipedia File: page — all still en.wikipedia.org and all genuinely the bamboo grove. If you want strict single-article provenance, only the infobox photo qualifies; say the word and I'll drop or replace the other two.
  • Resolution is uneven. Images were captured at the sizes Wikipedia's article pages serve, mostly 250–500 px wide (Nijo's gate photo is 960 px). Higher-resolution originals exist on Wikimedia Commons if you need print-quality files.
  • Deduplication was by image URL, so no duplicates were collapsed or lost during the parallel writes.

The collection is available as the kyoto_image image collection — open Data/gallery to browse or export it.
